peerMapping.justification: The block uses XYZ100 as the single primary index hedge and five positive-weight single-name equity peers, with weights summing to exactly 1. The peer basket is weighted 75 percent to logic and AI compute semiconductors through NVDA, AMD and INTC, and 25 percent to memory and storage through MU and SNDK, matching MRVL's AI data-center, networking, custom silicon and storage exposure while avoiding non-semiconductor names. Displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is respected in USD millions: MRVL is 1.269 USD millions, NVDA is 3.384 USD millions, AMD is 1.180 USD millions, INTC is 6.434 USD millions, MU is 11.877 USD millions and SNDK is 31.164 USD millions. Liquidity sets capacity, but final weights still prioritize economic comparability, which is why highly liquid memory and storage names are included yet capped.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVDA is the closest available AI data-center semiconductor comparator: GPUs, networking and accelerated computing are driven by the same hyperscale capex cycle as Marvell's custom silicon, DSP and optical interconnect products. Its 24-hour perp liquidity is 3.384 USD millions versus 1.269 USD millions for MRVL, so it can carry the largest peer weight.

peers.name: Advanced Micro Devices
peers.reason: AMD has high economic comparability through data-center CPUs and GPUs tied to AI server demand. Its 24-hour perp liquidity is 1.180 USD millions, slightly below MRVL at 1.269 USD millions, so the weight is large for product fit but not above NVDA.

peers.name: Intel
peers.reason: INTC is less aligned because of client PCs, CPUs and foundry execution, but it remains a large diversified semiconductor issuer with the same broad chip-cycle and US large-cap trading factors. Its 24-hour perp liquidity is 6.434 USD millions, comfortably above MRVL's 1.269 USD millions, supporting a meaningful but secondary weight.

peers.name: Micron Technology
peers.reason: MU is very liquid at 11.877 USD millions of displayed 24-hour perp liquidity and has strong AI data-center memory exposure, but its commodity memory mix is less directly comparable than AI compute and networking silicon, so it is sized below NVDA and AMD.

peers.name: Sandisk
peers.reason: SNDK has the deepest displayed 24-hour perp liquidity in the peer set at 31.164 USD millions, but it is mainly NAND storage rather than MRVL's mixed-signal interconnect and custom silicon franchise, so high liquidity is not allowed to dominate the weight.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: XYZ100 is the cleanest primary hedge because it is classified as equity_index, tracks the Nasdaq-100 large-cap technology complex that dominates MRVL's market beta, and shows 21.944 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity. It is broader than DRAM, not leveraged like SOXL, and keeps more technology and semiconductor factor exposure than SP500.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; basket rebased to the target spot level at the first overlapping date

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by each peer's latest USD cash close; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot close

earningsOptions.source: consolidated listed-options chain, verified earnings calendars, and split-adjusted price history

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with verified calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
